FN-IDG96W6-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 22
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Representative Mark Gidley
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 03/21/2024
House Bill 22 as reported by the Committee on Education Policy would require each public
school in the state to have an assistant principal, contingent upon the availability of funds.
The cost to provide an assistant principal to each public school that does not currently have an
assistant principal would be an estimated $54.5 million annually, if funded by the Foundation
Program from the Education Trust Fund.
According to the State Department of Education, 320 schools currently do not have an assistant
principal.
